newsitem.title: USA: GM to sponsor women's basketball league, theater.
newsitem.headline: GM to sponsor women's basketball league, theater.

text.p: General Motors Corp., aiming to boost its image in sports and entertainment, said Monday it will be the exclusive automotive sponsor of the new Women's National Basketball Association and a massive Sony theater complex in suburban Detroit.

The three-year WNBA deal, which starts when the league's inaugural season tips off on June 21, gives GM car and truck advertising exclusivity across all three of the league's national television networks -- NBC, ESPN and Lifetime.
GM said it also will use the WNBA logo and the title 'Official Car and Truck' of the WNBA in advertising.
The new women's league has chartered teams in eight major cities, featuring four players from the 1996 U.S. Olympic Team and Olympians from five other countries.

In a separate agreement with Sony's Loeks-Star Theaters joint venture, GM will be the exclusive automotive sponsor of the new Star Southfield Entertainment Complex, a 20-screen, 200,000-square-foot complex scheduled to open in May in Southfield, Mich.

The complex will seat 6,000 in stadium-style theaters and will include several themed restaurants and entertainment-related stores. GM will have brand exposure throughout the complex, including information kiosks and displays of new car models.

"Our sponsorships with the WNBA and Sony extend GM's commitment to identify fresh, compelling ways to showcase our company and its brands to consumers," said Phil Guarascio, GM's vice president of North American advertising.
"In each case, we plan to establish a highly relevant experience that encourages customers to connect with our brands on their own terms," Guarascio said in a statement.
GM said the theater complex will draw more than 3 million patrons a year -- more than other famous Detroit-area venues, including Greenfield Village, Tiger Stadium or the Palace of Auburn Hills.
The efforts are a part of a broad GM effort to expose consumers to its brands and products in fun, low-key environments.

The automaker also is working on a new ride and attraction at Walt Disney Co.'s Epcot Center in Orlando, Fla., opening this spring, called Test Track. Disney also assisted in revamping GM's showroom on Fifth Avenue in New York.
GM's stock edged up 37.5 cents to $57.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
